why: Gentle ground holds rain long enough to soak in; steep ground sheds it as runoff (Nijesh 2024; Joshi 2024). Weight 25 -> 20 (23 Oct 2026) to make room for soil depth.

Forest litter and roots let water in; built-up and bare ground seal or crust the surface (ESA WorldCover 2021). In Tehri district, Sentinel-2 NDVI (Oct-Nov 2025, 20 m) splits tree cover into dense, open and sparse; elsewhere tree cover scores 0.9 (density not known). NDVI cut-offs are provisional.
How easily the mapped rock passes water through pores and fractures (GSI NGDR lithology; SOP ch. 3).

Fractures along faults and lineaments carry water down into the rock (Rathi 2021; ICIMOD 2018). Distance to the nearest GSI fault, GSI Bhukosh mapped lineament (1:250k: joints, fractures, shear zones) or DEM lineament.

How fast rain soaks into the top 30 cm of soil: sandy and stony soils take water in fast, clayey soils slowly (ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, 250 m; texture classes after USDA hydrologic soil groups). Weight 15 -> 10 (23 Oct 2026): soil depth is now its own factor.

class: Stony soil (coarse fragments 35% or more): added

why: Deeper soil over the rock stores more rain and lets it seep down slowly; thin soil sheds it as runoff (SoilGrids 2017 depth to bedrock, 250 m, capped at 200 cm; model estimate).
